common_name: Praha Gladiolus (Deep Velvety Red Exhibition Gladiolus)

planting.note: Plant corms 4 inches deep in full sun after the danger of frost has passed, and stagger plantings every two weeks for a longer bloom season. Praha, a Czech-bred exhibition cultivar, bears large, velvety deep red flowers on tall spikes.

directions: Praha, bred in the Czech Republic and long popular on the exhibition show bench, bears large, velvety deep-red florets closely set on tall, straight spikes, a saturated color prized for its clarity rather than any dark overtones. Plant corms in well-drained soil and stake or plant in blocks to support the tall flower spikes, which open from the bottom up over several weeks. Cut spikes for indoor arrangements once the lowest two or three florets show color, leaving at least four leaves on the plant to recharge the corm. In colder zones, lift and store corms after foliage yellows in fall.

common_name: Spic and Span Gladiolus (Classic Ruffled Clear Pink Gladiolus)

planting.note: Plant corms 4 inches deep in full sun after the danger of frost has passed, and stagger plantings every two weeks for a longer bloom season. Spic and Span is a long-grown exhibition favorite with clear pink, ruffled florets closely spaced on the spike.

directions: Spic and Span is a long-established exhibition and cut-flower cultivar bearing clear, even pink florets with softly ruffled edges, set close together on the spike for a full, uniform look prized at gladiolus shows. Plant corms in well-drained soil and stake or plant in blocks to support the tall flower spikes, which open from the bottom up over several weeks. Cut spikes for indoor arrangements once the lowest two or three florets show color, leaving at least four leaves on the plant to recharge the corm. In colder zones, lift and store corms after foliage yellows in fall.

directions: Amsterdam is a Dutch-bred, large-flowered cultivar grown widely in the commercial cut-flower trade for its pure white florets and unusually tall, sturdy spikes that hold up well in transport and floral arrangements. Plant corms in well-drained soil and stake or plant in blocks to support the tall flower spikes, which open from the bottom up over several weeks. Cut spikes once the lowest two or three florets show color, leaving at least four leaves on the plant to recharge the corm. In colder zones, lift and store corms after foliage yellows in fall.

Friendship, a mid-20th-century American introduction, bears warm salmon-orange florets and was once among the most widely grown commercial cut-flower gladiolus in the United States.

directions: Friendship is a mid-20th-century American cultivar whose warm, salmon-orange florets made it one of the most heavily planted commercial cut-flower gladiolus of its era, a variety still grown today by home gardeners for its reliable vigor and floriferousness. Plant corms in well-drained soil and stake or plant in blocks to support the tall flower spikes, which open from the bottom up over several weeks. Cut spikes for indoor arrangements once the lowest two or three florets show color, leaving at least four leaves on the plant to recharge the corm. common_name: Little Darling Gladiolus (Classic Miniature Salmon-Pink Gladiolus)

planting.note: Plant corms 3-4 inches deep in full sun after the danger of frost has passed. Little Darling, a classic 1950s miniature introduction, bears ruffled salmon-pink florets with a creamy-yellow throat on slender, self-supporting spikes.

directions: Little Darling is a classic miniature cultivar dating to the 1950s, bearing ruffled, salmon-pink florets with a soft creamy-yellow throat on slender spikes that rarely need staking, unlike full-size grandiflorus gladiolus. Its smaller scale makes it well suited to mixed perennial borders and smaller cutting gardens where a 4-foot spike would overwhelm the planting. Cut spikes once the lowest florets open, leaving at least four leaves on the plant to recharge the corm. In colder zones, lift and store corms after foliage yellows in fall.

common_name: Amanda Mahy Gladiolus (Butterfly-Type Salmon-Pink with Maroon Blotch)

planting.note: Plant corms 3-4 inches deep in full sun 2 weeks before to at the last frost date; nanus types tolerate cooler soil than grandiflorus hybrids. Amanda Mahy bears salmon-pink flowers marked with a deep maroon blotch on the lower petals.

directions: Amanda Mahy is an early-flowering Gladiolus nanus (butterfly-type) cultivar bearing soft salmon-pink florets marked with a bold, deep maroon blotch on the lower petals, a striking contrast that has earned it long-standing garden merit recognition in Europe. It is hardier and more compact than tall grandiflorus hybrids, blooming several weeks earlier and rarely needing staking. Plant corms in free-draining soil and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigorous flowering. In zones colder than its hardiness range, lift corms after foliage fades and store them frost-free over winter.

common_name: Christabel Gladiolus (Butterfly-Type Orange-Red with Cream Blotch)

planting.note: Plant corms 3-4 inches deep in full sun 2 weeks before to at the last frost date; nanus types tolerate cooler soil than grandiflorus hybrids. Christabel bears bright orange-red flowers with a creamy-white throat blotch.

directions: Christabel is an early-flowering Gladiolus nanus (butterfly-type) cultivar with vivid orange-red florets set off by a creamy-white throat blotch, a widely grown and long-established selection that has held a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit for its reliable garden performance. Its compact, self-supporting habit and earlier bloom time make it a good companion for late spring perennials well before tall grandiflorus gladiolus come into flower. Plant corms in free-draining soil and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor. In zones colder than its hardiness range, lift and store corms frost-free over winter.

common_name: Impressive Gladiolus (Butterfly-Type Soft Pink Bicolor Gladiolus)

planting.note: Plant corms 3-4 inches deep in full sun 2 weeks before to at the last frost date; nanus types tolerate cooler soil than grandiflorus hybrids. Impressive bears soft pink flowers with a darker rose-pink throat blotch.

directions: Impressive is an early-flowering Gladiolus nanus (butterfly-type) cultivar bearing soft pink florets highlighted by a deeper rose-pink throat blotch, a subtler color combination than many butterfly gladiolus that reads well in informal cottage-style plantings. Like other nanus types, it is hardier and shorter than grandiflorus hybrids and blooms noticeably earlier in the season. Plant corms in free-draining soil in full sun and divide congested clumps every few years to keep flowering strong. In zones colder than its hardiness range, lift and store corms frost-free over winter.

common_name: Alice Wright Gladiolus (Butterfly-Type Cream with Maroon Blotch)

planting.note: Plant corms 3-4 inches deep in full sun 2 weeks before to at the last frost date; nanus types tolerate cooler soil than grandiflorus hybrids. Alice Wright bears creamy-white flowers marked with a deep maroon throat blotch.

directions: Alice Wright is an early-flowering Gladiolus nanus (butterfly-type) cultivar bearing creamy-white florets marked with a bold, deep maroon blotch in the throat, a high-contrast pairing that stands out in a mixed spring border. It shares the compact, hardy habit typical of nanus hybrids, needing no staking and tolerating cooler soils at planting than tall grandiflorus types. Plant corms in free-draining soil in full sun and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigorous flowering. In zones colder than its hardiness range, lift and store corms frost-free over winter.

directions: Charm is a long-cultivated Gladiolus nanus (butterfly-type) selection bearing rose-pink florets with a small, deeper pink to maroon marking in the throat, one of the older named butterfly gladiolus still grown for its dependable, early-season display. Its short, sturdy spikes need no staking and its earlier bloom time lets it fill the gap between late spring bulbs and the main gladiolus season. Plant corms in free-draining soil in full sun and divide congested clumps every few years to keep flowering strong. In zones colder than its hardiness range, lift and store corms frost-free over winter.
